title: Aligning the Objective of LLM-based Program Repair
datasets: DebugBench: 590 bugs across C++, Java, Python 3; evaluation uses verified patches from unseen LeetCode tests
task: LLM automated program repair; align decoder-only completion objective by generating a complete refined function and let LLM locate/repair within function using artifacts, without statement-level FL.
input_setting: Buggy function, function-level localization; one-shot fixed example, optional function docs, failing tests and error messages; up to 10 complete-function candidates, validate by test suite and manual semantic-equivalence check for plausible Defects4J patches.
author_relationship_evidence: Paper footnote says source and results are publicly available at the exact D4C repo; README names paper and documents D4C, its model, datasets, scripts and archived results.
license: MIT License (GitHub API and root LICENSE).
exact_models: Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1 local checkpoint; paper reports 8xA100 server
weights_status: GPT-4-0613 hosted/paid API; Mixtral open weights but 8xA100 recommended. No fine-tuning reported.
evaluation_route: MIT repo includes data extraction, prompt construction, D4J/DebugBench generators, validator, benchmark artifacts, and archived patch/evaluation CSVs. Archived D4J correct_id list has 180 IDs; D4J GPT evaluation CSV has 437 rows; each DebugBench model eval CSV has 1,770 rows. README includes Defects4J setup and warns v3.0 changed/deprecated cases, and requires LeetCode cookies for DebugBench validation. Requirements are pinned; no code was executed or API called.
blockers: D4C is APR, not reproduction test generation or root-cause diagnosis; it uses pass/fail suites and outputs code patches, not tests or causal labels.
GPT-4-0613 is a historical paid endpoint; exact availability/API settings need checking. Mixtral rerun requires large local model serving (paper used 8xA100). No API calls were made.
Defects4J source/version compatibility: paper uses v1.2/v2.0, while README warns v3.0 removes/adds cases; retain archived 437-row results or reconstruct the historical setup.
DebugBench evaluation requires LeetCode account cookies and its external online judge; author archives are available but live reevaluation is operationally sensitive.
Paper cost unit is ambiguous: it reports $0.023 per patch and 10 samples per bug, then says $0.23 “for the entire dataset”; likely per bug but the paper wording does not state total clearly.
concept_fit: Moderate support for fault-localization and context studies on Defects4J; no manually annotated root-cause taxonomy and no test generation. The paper tests whether artifact-driven direct debugging can replace exact buggy-hunk localization.
recommendation: A reproducible, licensed APR implementation with useful Defects4J and cross-language DebugBench archives. Use it as support for perfect-vs-function-level FL and objective alignment, not as the main test-generation method or a root-cause label source. Cached outputs aid score audit; exact generation remains conditional on historical GPT API/compute and D4J version setup.
